# TCUQ offline prototype — results

**Verdict: DROP. Do not port to the phone tier.**

**Scope: SYNTHETIC-ONLY.** All sequences are generated by
`tools/train_disturbance_clf.py`'s own event generators (seeded;
dev seed 101, test seed 202, shifted seed 303). No recorded
Outride sequences exist. Posterior streams are simulated online
typing: each event's dip series is classified at prefix windows
(4 Hz steps, capped at 64 steps, final step = full event), using
the SHIPPED `disturbance_clf` weights frozen (forward pass verified
bit-exact against `test/ai_golden.json`, max abs diff ~1.6e-17).
Results measure the "prefix-typing + monitor" system, not the
shipped event classifier's whole-event accuracy.

## Headline numbers (test set, 1000 sequences, 51,643 scored steps)

| Metric | TCUQ (naive) | TCUQ (transient-aware) | Max-conf baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step failure detection AUROC (paper's metric) | 0.820 | 0.820 | **0.849** |
| Step failure detection AUPRC | 0.530 | 0.522 | **0.548** |
| Sequence trouble separation AUROC (INTERFERENCE/FAULT vs PASSING/LINGERING) | 0.332 | 0.339 | 0.330 |
| Sequence trouble separation AUPRC | 0.464 | 0.467 | 0.458 |

An AUROC of 0.33 on trouble separation is *worse than chance* —
and the baseline is equally bad (0.330). This is not a TCUQ
implementation failure; it is a domain mismatch (see below).

## Why it fails: FAULT is the most consistent class in the taxonomy

Mean sequence r by class (transient-aware variant):

| Class | Mean sequence r |
|---|---|
| PASSING | 0.336 |
| LINGERING | 0.386 |
| INTERFERENCE | 0.403 |
| FAULT | **0.251 (lowest)** |

A FAULT is a pinned flatline by definition. Its prefix posteriors
are rock-stable and confident from the first window, so every
temporal-consistency signal reports "certain." Temporal consistency
measures *stability*, not *correctness* — and in Outride's
taxonomy the trouble classes are not unstable classes. INTERFERENCE
flicker is only mildly unstable (0.403 vs LINGERING 0.386), and
FAULT actively inverts the signal. No confidence-based score can
separate these classes, because INTERFERENCE/FAULT are legitimate,
confident in-distribution diagnoses of the shipped classifier —
not cases where the classifier is unsure. The monitor's abstain
semantics do not map onto "withhold INTERFERENCE/FAULT labels":
those labels *are* the information.

Per-signal sequence AUROCs for trouble separation confirm no
single signal rescues it: D 0.338, instability 0.459, inconsistency
0.428–0.436, confidence/margin proxy 0.332. The fitted combiner
leans on D and the confidence proxy (naive weights
[6.06, 0.84, −1.53, 5.93]), i.e. on quantities the baseline
already captures — which is why step failure detection also loses
to max-confidence (0.820 vs 0.849).

## Operational rule check (abstain at dev 90th percentile of mean r)

| Class | Flag rate (naive) | Flag rate (transient-aware) | Kept final-typing acc. | No-abstain acc. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PASSING | 0.141 | 0.114 | 0.976 | 0.952 |
| LINGERING | 0.084 | 0.084 | 0.983 | 0.972 |
| INTERFERENCE | 0.176 | 0.180 | 0.947 | 0.908 |
| FAULT | 0.000 | 0.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |

Kept accuracy rises slightly, but the rule does not selectively
catch trouble: FAULT is *never* flagged, and INTERFERENCE is
flagged at barely above the PASSING rate. The gain is just
"abstain on uncertain steps," which a plain max-confidence
threshold already provides without monitor complexity. The
transient-aware variant (flip-rate persistence) helps the trap
only marginally — PASSING flag rate 14.1% → 11.4% — and changes
no verdict.

## Shifted-set check (paper's CID claim, Outride-flavored)

Mean sequence r, transient-aware variant, vs clean movers (0.364):

| Shift | Mean r | Baseline (1 − maxprob) |
|---|---|---|
| gain ×1.6 | 0.343 | 0.059 |
| spikes overlay | 0.369 | 0.076 |
| mixed (mover + sine flicker) | 0.370 | 0.081 |
| square-wave interference (novel family) | 0.400 | 0.082 |

Shifted movers score essentially the same as clean movers
(gain-shifted movers score *lower*). The monitor does not detect
these shifts on Outride data.

## Coverage gap (monitor blind spot)

65 of 250 test PASSING sequences produced zero scored steps: the
shortest genuine passes yield fewer than 5 prefix steps, and the
monitor needs lag-4 history before it emits anything. The monitor
is blind exactly where the fastest passes live.

## What would change this verdict

1. Real recorded sequences (not synthetic) showing a different
   stability structure — but the FAULT-stability mechanism is
   structural (flatline ⇒ stable posteriors by construction),
   not a synthetic artifact, so this is unlikely to reverse.
2. A redefined monitor target: flagging *wrong* typings within
   mover classes only, rather than separating trouble classes.
   Even there, the monitor currently loses to max-confidence,
   so it would need a new signal, not a retune.
3. A different uncertainty question entirely (e.g. detecting
   WiIntruder-style perturbation), which this prototype did not
   test — perturbation was not simulated here.

## Guardrail (carried through the whole evaluation)

Abstention in this framing withholds ONLY the type label +
confidence. It NEVER gates the deterministic tripwire alert, which
is not modeled or touched by this prototype in any way.

## Reproduce

```
~/workspace/.mlvenv/bin/python evaluate.py   # regenerates results.json
```

Seeds: dev 101, test 202, shifted 303; 250 sequences/class for
dev and test; 100 per shift per mover class + 100 square-wave
interference. Monitor defaults: lags {1,2,4} with 1/l weights,
λ = 0.7, quantile α = 0.1, window W = 16, margin blend α_m = 0.5.
